scenario.feature: Send email on the user's behalf; optionally read the inbox

summary.text: Google fully supports third-party OAuth 2.0 for server-side applications accessing the Gmail API.
Developers can register an OAuth app in Google Cloud by setting the consent screen to External or Internal user types.

Sending email requires the sensitive scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send; reading the inbox requires the restricted scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly which requires CASA Tier 2 third-party security assessment.
External customer deployments requesting sensitive scopes trigger Google's OAuth app verification and security assessments.

next_action.instruction: Create a Google Cloud project and configure the OAuth consent screen with external user type.
next_action.success_condition: A Google Cloud project is created and the OAuth consent screen is configured.

paths.name: Testing & Development Mode
paths.applicability: Suitable for initial development and testing with up to 100 test users without immediate app verification.

gates.note: Not mandatory for initial testing using test users under the testing publishing status.

limits.text: Limited to up to 100 test users for apps in Testing publishing status.

steps.title: Create Test Credentials
steps.instructions: Create an OAuth client ID in the Google Cloud Console and configure a test consent screen adding test users.
steps.success_condition: OAuth client ID is created and test users are added.

waiting.explanation: No waiting period for testing setup.

paths.name: Production Deployment for External Customers
paths.applicability: Required when deploying the feature to external customers utilizing sensitive Gmail scopes.

gates.note: Required for external users requesting sensitive or restricted Gmail scopes.

Restricted scopes like gmail.readonly require an annual Cloud Application Security Assessment (CASA Tier 2) by an authorized third-party assessor. Sensitive-only scopes like gmail.send require standard Google OAuth verification.
Restrictions apply on AI/ML model training using restricted scope user data without explicit consent.

prerequisites.text: Google Cloud project with OAuth consent screen set to External user type.
Compliance with Google API Services User Data Policy.

steps.title: Configure Production OAuth and Submit for Verification
steps.instructions: Implement server-side authorization flow, configure production OAuth client credentials, and submit the app for Google OAuth verification. If requesting restricted scopes (gmail.readonly), complete the third-party CASA Tier 2 security assessment.
steps.success_condition: Verification and security assessment submission are completed.

effort.explanation: Estimated effort to implement server-side flow and prepare verification submission materials.

waiting.explanation: Google OAuth app verification and security assessment typically range from 2 to 4 weeks.

conflicts.topic: Precise classification and assessment triggers for `gmail.readonly` and `gmail.send`
conflicts.description: S1 states that `gmail.send` and `gmail.readonly` are sensitive and require a security assessment, whereas S2 classifies them under standard sensitive/restricted scope verification tracks.
conflicts.resolution: Both apply depending on whether Google classifies the particular deployment as requiring standard sensitive verification or a full CASA assessment; S1 reflects tighter enforcement of security assessments for external customer-facing apps requesting mailbox access.

claims.text: Third-party OAuth 2.0 is fully supported by Google for web, server-side, and installed applications accessing the Gmail API.
claims.conditions: When accessing Gmail API via web, server-side, or installed applications.

claims.text: Any developer with a Google Cloud account may register an OAuth app; registration requires creating a Google Cloud project, configuring the OAuth consent screen, and setting the user type to External or Internal.
claims.conditions: When registering an OAuth app in Google Cloud.

claims.text: The smallest documented permissions for sending email and optionally reading the inbox are https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send (classified as sensitive) and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly (classified as restricted).
claims.conditions: When requesting permissions to send mail and read the inbox.

claims.text: For external customers, requesting sensitive scopes triggers standard Google OAuth app verification; requesting restricted scopes like gmail.readonly requires an annual Cloud Application Security Assessment (CASA Tier 2) by an authorized third-party assessor.
claims.conditions: When requesting sensitive scopes for users outside the Google Workspace organization.

claims.text: To get a first test connection working, a developer creates credentials in the Google Cloud Console, configures a test consent screen, and adds test users (up to 100 users for apps in Testing publishing status).
claims.conditions: When using apps in Testing publishing status.

claims.text: Your app needs Google OAuth app verification if it is set to External user type on the OAuth consent screen and requests any sensitive or restricted Gmail scopes from users outside your own Google Workspace organization.
claims.conditions: When app is set to External and requests sensitive or restricted scopes.
